I've written all 678 ids across `output-1.json` (x001–x226), `output-2.json` (x227–x452) and `output-3.json` (x453–x678). 565 are converted to class chains and 113 are skipped, each with a reason. I only had file read/write tools here, so I couldn't parse the JSON or run any chain against a device. Running each part through a JSON parser before merging would be a worthwhile check.

**Why locators were skipped:**
- **Moving sideways or up the tree** (most skips): `following-sibling`, `preceding-sibling`, `following::`, `parent::` and `..`. Class chain can only step down to children or descendants.
- **Position within each parent:** in XPath, `//X[2]`, `//X[last()]` and `child::*[1]` mean "the nth X under each parent". A class chain index counts across all matches combined, so the result is different.
- **Direct-child conditions:** `[XCUIElementTypeButton]` and `[./Button[...]]` require a direct child. The class chain `$…$` check accepts any descendant, so it would match too much. Also skipped: `count()=2`, nearest ancestor `ancestor::Cell[1]`, and ranges like `position() <= n`.
- **Unions that can't be merged into one path,** and conditions that depend on whether some element exists anywhere on the page (x058, x539).
- **Locators that are invalid or never match:**
  - XPath 2.0 functions (`matches`, `ends-with`, `lower-case`, `tokenize` and similar), which the driver's XPath 1.0 engine rejects.
  - `text()` and `@text`: iOS elements have no text, so these never match anything.
  - Made-up types `XCUIElementTypeLabel` and `XCUIElementTypeAny`.
  - Two malformed strings (x091, x530).
- **Numeric comparisons** on `@x` and `@value`: these could give different results from the class chain version (for example with fractional coordinates).

**Conversion choices worth checking:**
- `//*` becomes `**/*`, `(…)[last()]` becomes `[-1]` and `[last()-1]` becomes `[-2]`. `@enabled="true"` becomes `enabled == 1`.
- **`contains(@type,"…")`:** this becomes the element type directly. x332 keeps `type CONTAINS "XCUIElementTypeText"` because it covers both TextField and TextView.
- **x294 `@enabled=true()`:** XPath treats this as "the enabled attribute exists", which every element has. So it matches every button and the result is `**/XCUIElementTypeButton`.
- **x365 `@label!="a"`:** I added `label != nil` because the XPath doesn't match elements that have no label.
- **Text-matching rewrites (x009, x447, x602):**
  - x009: `translate(...)` lowercasing became a case-insensitive `CONTAINS[c]`.
  - x447: `normalize-space` became a regex that allows the same whitespace.
  - x602: `string-length(@label) > 3` became `MATCHES "(?s).{4,}"`.
- **Unverified details:** these are my best understanding of how the driver handles them, but untested:
  - the escaped backtick written as two backticks (x334);
  - the backslash in x651;
  - the line breaks in x330, x484 and x575, which I kept as real newlines;
  - `hittable`, `selected`, `accessible` and `placeholderValue`, which I assumed work in class chain conditions as they do in the page source.
